This guide shows how to make a randomisation list with **randolist**,
following the OUCRU SOP *PR-BST-DM-001 Creating Randomisation Lists* (v008).
The package is a revision of the legacy `createRandoListNew.R`: for the same
seed and settings it gives **the same list**, so existing studies can switch
without their lists changing.

```{r}
library(randolist)
```

## Who does what

The SOP keeps the trial statistician blinded by splitting the work:

| Step | Who | What |
|---|---|---|
| 4.1.b | Statistician (RA) | Writes the code and makes a **dummy** list (seed known, arms named `*_Dummy`). |
| 4.1.c | Head of Biostatistics | Reviews and approves the code. |
| 4.1.e–f | Pharmacist | Sets the dummy flag to `FALSE`, replaces the seed with a new random seed, runs the code. |
| 4.1.g | Pharmacist | Checks the final list (e.g. balance within blocks) and stores it in the secure Pharmacy folder. |

Only the seed and the dummy flag differ between the dummy and the final code.
Everything below is designed so that this switch cannot go wrong silently.

## 1. The statistician's dummy code

Put these settings at the very top of the study script. `DUMMY` controls the arm
names and the output file names; `check_final_setup()` stops the final run if the
seed was not changed.

```{r}
DUMMY      <- TRUE        # pharmacist: set to FALSE
DUMMY_SEED <- 20261104    # seed of the dummy list (known to the statistician)
SEED       <- DUMMY_SEED  # pharmacist: replace with generate_seed() output

check_final_setup(dummy = DUMMY, seed = SEED, dummy_seed = DUMMY_SEED)
arm_names <- dummy_arm_names(c("Dex", "Pla"), dummy = DUMMY)
arm_names
```

Now generate the list. Use the SOP block lengths explicitly (4 and 6 with
probabilities 0.75 and 0.25 for two arms) and make the list at least twice as
long as the largest anticipated stratum.

```{r}
rl <- createRandoList(
  nPat             = 200,          # 100 anticipated patients x 2
  arms             = 2,
  arm_names        = arm_names,
  strata           = c(HTD = "001"),
  blocklength      = c(4, 6),
  blocklength_prob = c(0.75, 0.25),
  seed             = SEED
)
head(rl, 8)
```

Passing `seed` inside the call is the same as calling `set.seed(SEED)` just
before it, but makes it impossible to forget. The function also remembers how
the list was made:

```{r}
str(attr(rl, "rando_info")[c("seed", "rng_kind", "R_version", "blocklength_prob")])
```

## 2. Check the list

`check_rando_list()` confirms that randomisation numbers are unique and that
every complete block is balanced. The last block may be incomplete because the
list is cut at `nPat`.

```{r}
check_rando_list(rl)
```

## 3. Write it with SOP file names

`write_rando_list()` builds the file name from the study, the dummy flag, the
MonthYear and the R version (SOP 4.1.b), and writes a log with the MD5 sum of
each file and the session information.

```{r}
out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "24EI_Nov2026")   # in practice: the study subfolder
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
files <- write_rando_list(rl, dir = out_dir, study = "24EI", dummy = DUMMY,
                          overwrite = TRUE)
basename(files$file)
```

It refuses combinations that would break blinding:

```{r, error = TRUE}
# arm names say "Dummy" but the flag says final
write_rando_list(rl, dir = out_dir, study = "24EI", dummy = FALSE)

# a final list may not go to a Biostatistics folder
biostat <- file.path(tempdir(), "BIOSTATISTICS")
dir.create(biostat, showWarnings = FALSE)
final_like <- createRandoList(20, arm_names = c("Dex", "Pla"), seed = 583920175)
write_rando_list(final_like, dir = biostat, study = "24EI", dummy = FALSE)
```

## 4. What the pharmacist changes

The pharmacist receives the approved script and changes **only** the three lines
at the top (and the output folder):

```r
DUMMY      <- FALSE
DUMMY_SEED <- 20261104          # leave as is
SEED       <- 583920175         # from generate_seed(), not a memorable number
out_dir    <- "<secure Pharmacy folder>"
```

Get the new seed once with:

```{r}
generate_seed()
```

Then run the script in a clean session so no copy of the list is left in a
workspace file: `Rscript --vanilla 24EI_randolist.R`. If the seed was not
changed, the script stops:

```{r, error = TRUE}
check_final_setup(dummy = FALSE, seed = 20261104, dummy_seed = 20261104)
```

Keep the final code, CSV, log and PDF together in the Pharmacy folder. The log
contains the seed, so it must not be copied to the Biostatistics folder. When
making the PDF for pharmacy procedures, leave out the `block_number` and
`permute.block` columns: they reveal the block structure.

A template script with all of this is installed with the package:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
file.copy(system.file("templates", "rando_list_template.R", package = "randolist"),
          "24EI_randolist.R")
```

## Stratified randomisation

Combine strata with `composite_strata()`. Each stratum gets its own blocks; the
stratum code is part of the randomisation number.

```{r}
strata <- composite_strata(site = c(HCMC = "1", HN = "2"),
                           age  = c(Child = "C", Adult = "A"))
strata

srl <- createRandoList(nPat = c(60, 40, 80, 40), strata = strata,
                       arm_names = arm_names, blocklength = c(4, 6),
                       blocklength_prob = c(0.75, 0.25), seed = SEED)
names(srl)
head(srl$HCMC.Child, 4)
```

By default the strata are generated one after another from a single random
stream (as in the legacy code), so changing the size of one stratum changes the
strata after it. If a stratum may need to be extended later, use
`seed_per_stratum = TRUE`: stratum *i* then uses seed `SEED + i - 1` and the
strata no longer depend on each other.

```{r}
a <- createRandoList(c(20, 30), strata = c(A = "1", B = "2"), seed = SEED,
                     seed_per_stratum = TRUE, patid_format = list(width = 3, flag = "0"))
b <- createRandoList(c(50, 30), strata = c(A = "1", B = "2"), seed = SEED,
                     seed_per_stratum = TRUE, patid_format = list(width = 3, flag = "0"))
identical(a$B, b$B)
```

## Permuting patient numbers

`n.block_permute` shuffles the patient numbers within every *n* blocks, so the
numbers on the packs do not follow the allocation order. Be clear about which
order patients are enrolled in:

* if patients receive the **next row** of the list, balance holds at the end of
  every block, as usual;
* if patients receive the **next randomisation number**, the shuffled numbers
  define the sequence and balance is only guaranteed at the end of each group of
  `n.block_permute` blocks (with `Inf`, only at the end of the stratum).

```{r}
p <- createRandoList(24, arm_names = arm_names, blocklength = 4,
                     n.block_permute = 2, seed = SEED)
p[, c("pat_id", "block_number", "permute.block", "arm", "RanNo")]
```

## Reproducibility checklist

* Copy the package version (or the function file) used into the study folder;
  the log records `randolist` and R versions.
* Set the seed in the call (`seed =`) and keep `sample_kind` the same for the
  dummy and the final list. The default `"Rounding"` matches the legacy code;
  `"Rejection"` is R's current default and equally reproducible.
* Re-running the final code must give the same MD5 sum as in the log.
* The function restores your random number settings when it finishes, so code
  that runs after it is not affected.

## Differences from the legacy `createRandoListNew.R`

Same seed + same arguments give the same list, with these exceptions, which
are all deliberate:

* **Two bug fixes**, both only when patient numbers are permuted
  (`n.block_permute > 0`):
    * the legacy code could give a wrong or duplicated patient number when the
      last permutation group held a single patient (`sample(41, 1)` samples
      from `1:41`). The new code keeps the correct number; all other rows and
      the following strata are unchanged;
    * when all permutation groups had the same size, the legacy code stopped
      with "pat_id not found". The new code works.
* Lists whose randomisation numbers would not be unique are refused.
* Strata with fewer patients than arms (or none) are allowed.
* The caller's `sample.kind` is restored instead of being reset to `"default"`.

The package tests run the legacy file side by side with the new code over many
seeds and settings to confirm this.
